source_documents.title: Helically Flexible Boron‐Dipyrromethenes for Solution‐Processed Isotropic Films With Preserved Chiral Exciton Coupling

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, blocking meso-aryl rotation by replacing the mesop-tolyl groups of (S,S)-1 and (S,S)-2 with sterically hindered mesityl groups to generate (S,S)-3 and (S,S)-4 led to a substantial
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-1 vs (S,S)-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Locking the meso aryl raises fluorescence efficiency.

reference_evidence_units.quote: particularly in lowpolarity solvents (e.g., ϕflu = 0.17 for (S,S)-1 vs. ϕflu = 0.78 for (S,S)-3 in cyclohexane; see Figure 3).
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-1 vs (S,S)-3

reference_evidence_units.quote: Additionally, it is well established that meso-aryl “rotors” in BODIPYs—freely rotating aryl substituents at the BODIPY 8-position—promote non-radiative decay pathways enabled by conformational relaxation, thereby reducing luminescence efficiency
reference_evidence_units.subject: meso-aryl BODIPYs
reference_evidence_units.statement: Free meso-aryl rotation opens non-radiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Cited prior knowledge; not re-measured with viscosity here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This spectroscopic behavior is consistent with increasing contribution of a luminescent BODIPY-toBODIPY SBCT state—responsible for the short-wavelength absorption band and the quenching of the fluorescence response (Figure 3)—as the polarity of the medium increases
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Symmetry-breaking CT between the two BODIPYs quenches emission in polar solvents.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Expectedly, the fluorescence of (S,S)-4 shows a stronger dependence on solvent polarity, reflecting the presence of an overcrowded, mesitylbased diamine bridge, which favors BODIPY-to-BODIPY SBCT, particularly in polar solvents
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-4

reference_evidence_units.quote: new (S,S)-3 and (S,S)-4 exhibit the expected strong and sharp Vis positive couplets (Figure 4), demonstrating efficient intramolecular chiral exciton coupling between the involved BODIPY chromophores
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-3, (S,S)-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Exciton-coupled ECD couplet from the two BODIPYs.

reference_evidence_units.quote: is significantly higher than that of the diphenylated-bridge-based analogue (S,S)-3
reference_evidence_units.subject: (S,S)-4 vs (S,S)-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bridge crowding strengthens the exciton couplet (Δ[θ] 30 vs 12 x 10^6).

reference_evidence_units.quote: enabling chiral exciton coupling (e.g., positive ECD couplet for (M)-helicoBODIPYs).
reference_evidence_units.subject: helicoBODIPYs incl. (S,S)-1

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Meso aryl locked by mesityl, as in 3.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The overcrowded bridge favours BODIPY-to-BODIPY SBCT, giving the strongest polarity-dependent quenching.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Intramolecular exciton coupling between the two covalently linked BODIPYs (guideline §3.5 treats intramolecular excimers as AGGREGATE); the evidence is the ECD couplet. Strongest couplet of the series.
